clue.text: Linen flower on short American entertainer

indicators.note: something cut short has lost its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
Fanny Brice was an American comedian and singer

explanation.surface: A description of a flower pinned to the costume of a small American performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' wants to be a bloom; in crosswords it is often a river, here the Cam.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambric is a fine, closely woven white fabric originally made of linen, named after the town of Cambrai.

clue.text: Carbon residue on Jersey, perhaps, is a money-spinner

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
ash is what remains after burning
a Jersey is a breed of dairy cattle

explanation.surface: Soot left on a jersey somehow turns out to be lucrative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like a sweater or the Channel Island; it is the breed of cow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cash cow is a business or product that reliably generates profit, exactly what a money-spinner is.

clue.text: Tall grass labyrinth I entered

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it, so a letter is placed within a word

blocks.note: a labyrinth is a maze
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone describes walking into a maze cut through tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, maize mazes are a popular farm attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, or corn, is a cereal plant of the grass family that grows tall.

clue.text: Opening information about old physicist

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes around another

blocks.note: a rent is a tear or opening
O is the standard abbreviation for old
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Details released about a physicist of a former age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like the start of the clue's sense; it is a noun meaning a tear, and gen is British slang worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilhelm Roentgen was the German physicist who discovered X-rays in 1895.

clue.text: Gas a bird

blocks.note: first meaning: talk idly
second meaning: a small songbird such as the stonechat

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like gassing a bird; 'gas' is informal British for chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to talk casually and is also the name of several small songbirds.

clue.text: Summon gang during drink

indicators.note: something happening during another sits within it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: to sup is to drink
a crew is a gang

explanation.surface: Calling a gang together while they are having a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the sense found in the phrase 'screw up one's courage'.
explanation.definitionFit: To screw up courage is to summon or muster it, so the phrasal verb can mean summon.

clue.text: The gall of the rider!

blocks.note: surface reading: the cheek or nerve of a horseman
setter's reading: a gall is a sore made by chafing, here from sitting on a horse

explanation.walkthrough: Gall usually means impudence, but it is also a skin sore from rubbing, the sense meant here.
explanation.definitionFit: Riders get chafed and painful where they sit on a horse, a condition known by this two-word phrase.

clue.text: Material part of 29 tournament?

blocks.note: first meaning: the elastic substance from latex
second meaning: a set of games in the card game that is the answer to 29

explanation.surface: Some substance forms part of a sporting competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 across is ABRIDGE, whose card-game sense is BRIDGE; a rubber is a best-of-three set of games in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an elastic substance and also a series of games forming a unit of play in bridge or whist.

clue.text: Halt while changing admin staff here

indicators.note: changing letters alters their order, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Office workers are told to stop while things are being reorganised.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitehall is the London street lined with government ministries, so it stands for Britain's civil service administration.

clue.text: Fighters look around for shade

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: paras are paratroopers
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Soldiers scan their surroundings in search of some shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasol is a light umbrella carried to give protection from the sun.

clue.text: Drunk ape drinks aromatic liquid

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about out of order, so the following words are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tipsy monkey downs some fragrant fluid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drinks' looks like a verb with the ape as subject; it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikenard, or nard, is a fragrant ointment or oil prepared from a Himalayan plant, used since antiquity.

clue.text: One cuts a device that supports front of rusty pipe

indicators.note: something that cuts into another goes inside it
the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
I is the Roman numeral one
first letter of rusty

explanation.surface: A tool that holds up the end of a corroded pipe is being sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside BRA, then R is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A briar is a tobacco pipe carved from the root of the tree heath.

clue.text: Greek Island imports American produce

indicators.note: a place that imports takes things in, so a letter is brought inside

blocks.note: Crete is the largest Greek island
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A Greek island brings in fruit and vegetables from the USA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like a noun for farm goods; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To create is to bring something into existence, which is a verb sense of produce.

clue.text: With no idea how this puzzle started

blocks.note: first meaning: completely ignorant
second meaning: read literally, lacking clues, as a blank grid does before any are written

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into clue plus less: before the setter wrote the clues, the grid had none.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means having no understanding at all, and taken literally it means without any hints.

clue.text: Censor? Presumably Picasso had one for a period!

definitions.text: Presumably Picasso had one for a period!

blocks.note: first meaning: to cut or edit out material

blocks.clueFragment: Presumably Picasso had one for a period!
blocks.note: second meaning: a tool for drawing in his Blue Period, a joke on his years of blue paintings

explanation.walkthrough: Picasso's Blue Period (1901 to 1904) produced mostly blue-toned work, so he would whimsically have needed this implement.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors traditionally marked cuts with a coloured crayon, so the phrase came to mean censoring or deleting text.

clue.text: Drive to tour?

blocks.note: surface reading: a car journey taken to go sightseeing
setter's reading: drive as an inner urge, here the urge to roam

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' suggests motoring; it is the noun meaning a compelling desire.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderlust is a strong longing to travel and roam the world, an urge or impulse to go touring.

clue.text: Punk German hit is an awful experience

indicators.note: punk suggests something wild and anarchic, so the following letters are disordered

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A punk record that topped the German charts proves dreadful to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream, and by extension any dreadful or very unpleasant ordeal.

clue.text: Bouncer, say, heard to cry

indicators.note: heard means we go by what the ear catches, not the spelling

blocks.note: to bawl is to cry loudly

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman is said to have wept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman; here it is something that bounces.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is the classic example of a thing that bounces, hence 'say' marking an example.

clue.text: Bolt, say, front of stapler to machine in an office

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of stapler
a printer is standard office equipment

explanation.surface: Someone attaches a bolt to the front of a stapler and then to an office printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' looks like a fastener among the office kit; it is Usain Bolt, the Jamaican sprint champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Usain Bolt is the most famous example of a fast short-distance runner, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Kit — second for Manchester City

indicators.note: second points to the letter in position two of the following word

blocks.note: a rig is a set of gear or clothing
second letter of Manchester

explanation.surface: A note on a football club's strip, with a spare one kept for Manchester City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manchester City' reads as one football club; the words split, City alone being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital city of Latvia, on the Baltic coast.

clue.text: Is Roman Emperor following right Italian course?

indicators.note: following tells us which piece comes behind which, fixing their order

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
Otto was a Roman emperor for three months in AD 69

explanation.surface: A question about whether an emperor in Rome trails the correct path in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto was one of the short-lived emperors of the Year of the Four Emperors, AD 69.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a rice dish from northern Italy, served as a course of a meal.

clue.text: Expressionist movie plot is more complicated

indicators.note: making something complicated tangles it, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A film critic notes that an expressionist film's story is rather convoluted.
explanation.definitionFit: Metropolis is Fritz Lang's 1927 German silent science-fiction film, a landmark of Expressionist cinema.

clue.text: One leaves Tangiers resort for rum

indicators.note: something that leaves is gone, so that letter is taken out
read as re-sort, meaning sort again into a new order

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one, the letter removed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A person quits a Moroccan holiday destination in search of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place; read it as re-sort. 'Rum' is a drink in the surface but means odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is an old-fashioned British word for odd or peculiar, a synonym for strange.

clue.text: Girl after dad is a dish

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A daughter chasing her father is described as attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the girl's name behind PA. 'Dish' plays on its slang sense of an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish cooked with saffron, seafood or meat in a wide shallow pan.

clue.text: New statue I’d located

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the following letters form a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone reports having found a recently erected statue.
explanation.definitionFit: Situated means placed in a particular position, the same as located.

clue.text: Perhaps Rip Van Winkle’s cure?

blocks.note: surface reading: a remedy for the man who slept twenty years
setter's reading: he is a champion sleeper, and the cured fish shares its name with one who naps

explanation.walkthrough: To kip is British slang for to sleep, so the word fancifully means a sleeper; it is really a smoked herring, a cured fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A kipper is a split, salted and smoked herring, and jokingly one who kips, like the long sleeper Rip Van Winkle.

clue.text: Boastful United in bar at conclusion of championship

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter
in places one item inside another

blocks.note: last letter of championship
a rod is a bar
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A cocky United side celebrates in a pub after winning the title.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside ROD, and P comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Proud can mean having too high an opinion of oneself, hence boastful or arrogant.

clue.text: Bath with a bit of brass

blocks.note: a tub is a bath
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bathtub with a few brass fittings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' suggests metal fittings; it is the orchestra's brass section.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the largest, lowest-pitched instrument in the brass section of an orchestra.

clue.text: Follow first of tourists to bar

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: first letter of tourists
a rail is a bar

explanation.surface: Instructions to go after the leading holidaymakers heading for the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to follow them, often at a distance.

clue.text: Game nobleman has drink

blocks.note: a count is a European nobleman
to down is to drink in one go

explanation.surface: A sporting aristocrat enjoys a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Countdown is a long-running British TV word-and-numbers game show.
explanation.definitionFit: Countdown is a British television quiz programme, a game of letters and numbers puzzles.

clue.text: On the whole it protects clothes

blocks.note: first meaning: taking everything into account
second meaning: a loose coat worn over garments to keep them clean

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, it keeps your clothes safe.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb the word means generally, and as a noun it is a protective work garment worn over other clothing.

clue.text: Shorten a spanner

definitions.note: read as two words, a bridge

blocks.note: first meaning: cut down a text
second meaning: read as two words, a structure spanning a river

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanner' wants to be the wrench; it is something that spans a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book is to cut it down, and split in two the word gives a structure crossing a river or road.
